ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Legal framework comprises the Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law of 2007 (Law 188(I)/2007), as amended, implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843, and the Companies (Amendment) Law of 2021 (Law 114(I)/2021), which inserts Sections 61A to 61F into the Companies Law Cap. 113 and establishes the Register of Beneficial Owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or licensed notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Convention; Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HM Treasury OFSI Consolidated List, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, and the Cyprus domestic sanctions list maintained under Council of Ministers decisions. PEP status is determined under Article 2 of Law 188(I)/2007 using the FATF definitions of family members and close associates. Positive PEP or sanctions hits trigger enhanced due diligence, senior management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (DROCIP) electronic portal — www.companies.gov.cy
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in Greek or Latin characters. If Greek characters are used, a Latin transliteration must also be provided for EU BRIS registration. The legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is mandatory. Names must be distinctive and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, trade mark or protected public instrument.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Engineering (requires ETEK approval where implying regulated professional engineering activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or authorized corporate service provider may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar within 14 days of the refusal, explaining grounds for acceptance. If the refusal is confirmed, a new application with a distinct name may be filed. An administrative recourse may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Cyprus under Article 146 of the Cyprus Constitution within 30 days of the final refusal. Name reservations may be renewed by filing a new application before or after expiry, subject to continued availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable as a registered office address for company law purposes, provided it is a physical street address in Cyprus and not a PO Box, and the service provider is authorized to accept service of process. However, for banking onboarding and OECD/EU economic substance requirements, the company must have local staff, premises and decision-making capacity for the CAD/BIM outsourcing activity. A purely virtual arrangement without local substance will trigger enhanced AML/CFT review and may preclude Cyprus tax residence, causing denial of treaty benefits and increasing compliance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 12% annual probability for an unannounced on-site inspection for a non-regulated, low-risk CAD/BIM outsourcing company; probability rises to approximately 25% where the registered office is purely virtual or banking KYC flags substance concerns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law, Cap. 113 (as amended), ss. 3-9 relating to incorporation, memorandum, articles and certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Republic of Cyprus.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association, together with Form HE1 Declaration of Compliance; the resulting statutory instrument is the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar under section 9 of Companies Law, Cap. 113.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Cyprus private limited company; incorporation may proceed with one ordinary share of EUR 1.00 subscribed by each shareholder. No escrow or paid-up capital deposit is required for non-regulated professional services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers/members hereby subscribe to, take up, and hold the ordinary shares allocated against their names in the Memorandum of Association, and that the register of members be updated without delay. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be adopted at the address set out in the notice of registered office, Nicosia, Cyprus, and that the Company file the requisite notice with the Registrar. RESOLVED that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as the first Director, and that [Secretary Name] be appointed as Secretary. RESOLVED that the Directors are empowered to cause filings, open bank accounts, and instruct counsel to complete tax and licensing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve proposed company name and verify availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), Nicosia — Online Company Name Reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one primary and one alternate company name in Greek, with English transliteration, together with the intended business description. Obtain the DRCOR name reservation certificate before filing the incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Greek and English transliteration
Summary of intended CAD/BIM and engineering activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a second alternative through the same portal, or submit a formal written reconsideration to DRCOR within 14 days with supporting trade-mark search details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare constitutional documents and execute statutory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Appointed Cyprus advocate/notary public, on behalf of the future shareholders and first directors; final format checking by DRCOR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with Companies Law, Cap. 113. Each subscriber must execute the memorandum before a witness/notary, and the first directors/secretary must complete Form HE1 Declaration of Compliance and consent forms.
required_dossiers: Passport and proof of residential address for each subscriber and proposed officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the constitutional documents to remove any legal objections raised by counsel or DRCOR and re-execute/notarize the corrected documents before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), Nicosia — electronic filing desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed memorandum, articles, Form HE1, name reservation certificate and registered office consent into the DRCOR electronic system. The registrar examines the documents and, if satisfied, issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of name reservation certificate
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, provide the requested clarification or corrected document within 10 working days; an administrative appeal may be filed with DRCOR against any refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and establish statutory books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR); company's appointed corporate secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download or collect the Certificate of Incorporation and the stamped constitutional documents. Hold the first board meeting, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, issue share certificates and open the statutory registers of members, directors and charges.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected certificate from DRCOR if the company name, registration date or capital entries contain clerical errors; correct the statutory registers by board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company for tax, social insurance and VAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Republic of Cyprus; Social Insurance Services, Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, apply for the Cyprus Tax Identification Number through the Tax Department portal, register as an employer with Social Insurance Services, and complete a VAT application if taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold.
required_dossiers: Proof of physical office address (lease or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried for incomplete corporate details, file a supplemental sworn statement of officers and a certified English/Greek translation of the supporting documents within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure workplace, fire safety and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Labour Inspection, Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance; Fire Service, Cyprus Civil Defence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an inspection of the registered office, obtain fire safety clearance from the local Fire Service, confirm the building's structural load permits prescribed by the building management, and record the workplace risk assessment for employees.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection report or certificate
Office building lease and owner's consent/occupancy certificate
Workplace health and safety risk assessment
Employer registration with Social Insurance Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remedy any identified fire or occupational safety deficiencies and request a re-inspection; if the Fire Service declines clearance, file an appeal with the Civil Defence authority together with the corrected compliance report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7110 CAD/BIM and structural drafting is a professional office service and does not constitute an industrial establishment under the Cypriot industrial licensing rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no separate industrial operating permit is required. Ordinary workplace/fire safety clearances and any municipal business registration remain sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, Republic of Cyprus.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based professional services do not fall within the EIA project categories; no full Environmental Impact Assessment or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater must be discharged only to the municipal/public sewerage system in accordance with the local discharge consent; electronic waste (WEEE) and used printer toners must be consigned to authorized waste handlers; no volatile organic compounds, industrial effluent or combustion stack emissions are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the occupied office space; building owner's structural load confirmation for drafting workstations and server equipment; occupational health and safety inspection by the Department of Labour Inspection; no hazardous materials, chemical storage or dangerous processes are present, so no additional civil-defence licence is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus (Τμήμα Φορολογίας), Ministry of Finance; e-Filing portal: TAXISnet (https://taxisnet.mof.gov.cy); VAT Online Services and Cyprus Customs THIBCA declarations portal (https://customs.mof.gov.cy); Ariadne government e-Services portal (https://ariadne.mof.gov.cy).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cyprus-incorporated private limited company (HE77) is automatically issued a Tax Identification Code (TIC) upon incorporation by the Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver; the TIC is identical to the company's registration number and appears on the incorporation certificate. For VAT, the company files Form VAT 101 with the local VAT District Officer within 30 days of the month in which the €15,600 taxable turnover threshold is exceeded; non-resident applicants without a Cyprus establishment must register using Form VAT 103 and, if established outside the EU, must appoint a tax representative in Cyprus; the VAT registration certificate is issued with a Cyprus VAT number in the format CY12345678A. No separate federal or regional registration is required because Cyprus is a unitary jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: CY LTD is a Cyprus tax resident if managed and controlled in Cyprus (place-of-effective-management test). It is taxed at 12.5% corporate income tax on worldwide income, with territorial reliefs including the Participation Exemption (dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings), the Foreign Permanent Establishment exemption, and the Cyprus IP Nexus box. The entity is treated as a limited liability company, not a pass-through, and is subject to the general anti-avoidance and ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Elective mechanisms under the Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 and VAT Law N.95(I)/2000 include: (i) election to exempt foreign permanent establishment profits (forgoing foreign tax credits); (ii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election on new qualifying equity; (iii) group relief surrender of losses election; (iv) IP Nexus box computation election; (v) reorganization and demerger relief elections; (vi) deemed dividend distribution election and closed-company apportionment elections; (vii) VAT flat-rate small-enterprise scheme election; (viii) VAT option for intra-Community acquisitions and margin-scheme elections. Cyprus has no US-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is determined solely by Cypriot corporate and tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Cyprus Value Added Tax Law of 2000 (N.95(I)/2000), as amended, harmonised with the EU VAT Directive; administered by the Tax Department's VAT and Contributions Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €15,600 annual taxable turnover of goods and services; €10,251.61 threshold for intra-Community acquisitions; €35,000 for distance selling of goods to Cyprus consumers; no registration threshold applies to non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Cyprus where the reverse charge is unavailable; the application to register must be submitted within 30 days of exceeding the applicable threshold, with the effective registration date backdated to the day of exceedance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) fiscal clearance mandate is currently in force in Cyprus; there is no national digital stamp or immediate API clearance requirement for B2B invoices. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies to suppliers invoicing Cyprus public authorities through the national e-Invoice platform, using the European EN 16931 and Peppol BIS formats. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but must satisfy authenticity, integrity, and legibility requirements within EDI or PDF/XML custody; Cyprus is aligned with the EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age (ViDA) proposal, anticipating standardised e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting for intra-EU supplies from 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) exports of goods supplied by the exporter for removal from the EU within 90 days of the time of supply, including export under outward processing relief; (2) supplies of engineering, architectural, CAD/BIM drafting, and related professional services to a taxable person established in a third country or to a non-taxable person in a third country, where the place of supply rules place the supply outside Cyprus or specifically zero-rate it under Section 56 of the VAT Law; (3) supplies of services directly related to exported goods when the value is included in the customs value; (4) intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered EU customer, with evidence of the customer's valid VAT number and transport records. For CAD/BIM services supplied B2B to a foreign engineering contractor, the place of supply is normally the customer's country and the supply falls outside the scope of Cyprus VAT; where the customer is outside the EU, the supply is zero-rated or outside the scope, allowing recovery of input VAT under the 13th Directive procedure for non-established businesses.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD) lodged via Cyprus Customs THIBCA with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice (triplicate) for CAD/BIM drafting services and/or goods, specifying terms of delivery and currency
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note proving physical export and third-country destination
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice showing export payment received on a Cyprus bank account
Signed international sales or engineering services agreement with project scope, fee schedule, and Incoterms
Customer acceptance certificate or proof of delivery at the foreign project site, plus copy of customer VAT registration or third-country tax identification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Wrongful zero-rating is treated as non-remitted VAT and is clawed back through an assessment at 19% with default interest and a 10% late-payment surcharge under Section 107 of the VAT Law; the assessment window is 6 years for ordinary errors and 10 years for fraudulent or willful misconduct. Knowingly issuing a false export or zero-rating invoice is a criminal offence carrying fines and imprisonment under the VAT Law and Criminal Code, with joint liability for officers; input VAT recovered on zero-rated exports is recaptured if the 90-day export condition is not met or the documentary evidence is deficient. Cyprus imposes no exchange-control repatriation deadline for export proceeds; the 180-day convention reflects prudent cash management and transfer-pricing expectations, and unrepatriated trade receivables may be recharacterised as loans or deemed distributions under the Income Tax Law, triggering 12.5% corporate taxation and Defence Fund liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Kentriki Trapeza tis Kyprou); responsible for prudential supervision, payment systems oversight, foreign exchange statistics compilation, and balance-of-payments reporting under EU and national law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus is part of the euro area; the euro is fully convertible into any other currency on both capital and current accounts. EU free movement of capital applies, including for non-resident shareholders. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted in law, subject to delivery of statutory financial statements, tax compliance certificates, and bank AML/KYC documentation. Cyprus domestic withholding tax on dividends is 0% for non-residents, but dividend payments are reportable under DAC6, FATCA/CRS, and as exchange-control-related balance-of-payments transactions to the Central Bank of Cyprus.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no mandatory surrender requirements, statutory conversion ratios, or timelines requiring Cypriot exporters to repatriate or convert foreign currency receipts into euro. Export proceeds may be retained in freely convertible foreign-currency accounts at authorised Cypriot banks. However, all inward and outward payments exceeding EUR 10,000 must be reported for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, and invoices must be retained for AML and tax audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (EUR and foreign currency); segregated Capital Escrow Account for initial share capital injection
Operational Current Account and dedicated Sweeping Account for trade settlements
Corporate Operational Account; ancillary pooled banking facility for multi-currency receivables
Operational Account and Special Purpose Income Account for BIM service invoicing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium to Low for primary operating treasury. Cyprus recognises passported EU Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions regulated by the Central Bank of Cyprus and the European Banking Authority. Digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Paddle can be used for settlement of low-risk services and payment routing, but they do not substitute for a domestic credit institution for escrow, capital injection, high-value SWIFT traffic, or statutory audit trail. The primary entity account should be at a traditional tier-1 bank; a fintech EMI may be used as a supplementary disbursement rail, subject to bank pass-through KYC and contractual restrictions by the domestic banker.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Cypriot banks, as a rule, require the physical appearance of at least one director, the ultimate beneficial owner, and the signatory for the initial KYC interview at the Cypriot branch or in a foreign branch where individual exposure is approved. Fully remote onboarding is possible only for low-risk corporate clients with a clearly verifiable business model, provided that the director and UBO complete a live video-conference call before the Central Bank of Cyprus authorised compliance officer, submit notarised copies of passports and proof of residential address, and provide corporate documents apostilled under the Hague Convention. In practice, for a Cyprus private limited liability company engaged in civil infrastructure CAD/BIM outsourcing, a physical interview is highly recommended, and the bank may impose a secondary visit within twelve months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly non-resident ownership and lack of visible local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Release of audited financial statements, contract with an executive services provider, signed office lease in Cyprus, social insurance records for local employees, and a substance business plan confirming administrative and decision-making presence in Cyprus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or unspecified payment purpose description on inward wires from global engineering clients, particularly from jurisdictions with partial FATCA/CRS status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original signed master services agreement, detailed invoices with ISIC 7110 service descriptions, a schedule of each transaction referencing the underlying BIM project, and a written AML narrative from the external accountant demonstrating the client's source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transactional pattern or rapid withdrawal of funds following a large capital injection without corresponding procurement activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share capital inflow letter from the corporate accountant, capital contribution resolution, deposit confirmation receipts, and a projected 12-month cash-flow statement matched against payroll and subcontractor disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected use of altered identity documents or mismatch between registered director and actual UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry extract from the Department of Registrar of Companies showing director details, passport copies with certified translation, banking mandate signature card, and a compliance attestation executed by the physical director in the presence of the bank officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal-entity name or business purpose conflicting with bank's restricted sector list due to 'infrastructure' phrasing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A diagrammatic explanation that the entity is purely technology-aided engineering design and drafting, nothing involving real estate, construction equipment, or procurement, supported by the ISIC 7110 registration snippet and client contracts referencing CAD deliverables only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital contributions are routed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Instant Credit with a detailed beneficiary reference containing the company name, VAT/TIN number, and a purpose narrative 'ONLY CAPITAL INJECTION FOR SHAREHOLDER CONTRIBUTION' or the internationally accepted business purpose code 'ICAP' (Investment-related capital payment) where supported. The bank mandates submission of the board resolution, share certificate, written capital contribution agreement, and confirmation that the funds originate from an account held under the shareholder's name. For bookings above EUR 50,000, the bank may require a deposit of source documents and a statistical declaration to the Central Bank of Cyprus for balance-of-payments reporting. Any non-euro payment is settled at the ECB reference rate with no mandatory conversion; funds are held in the labelled Capital Escrow Account until utilisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for outsourced engineering services are cleared through SWIFT MT103 single credit transfers, MT202 for bank-to-bank reimbursements, and SEPA Instant Credit for eurozone counterparties. For larger civil infrastructure subcontracting, a commercially advised documentary letter of credit with transferable format may be opened through the Cypriot bank's trade finance desk; settlement terms are typically L/C at sight with full set of original transportation documents. Standard disbursement categories include payroll via local SEPA salary runs, software licensing fees to non-resident vendors, insurance premia, and subcontractor payments under a separate clearing arrangement. All outbound transactions above EUR 10,000 receive a unique payment purpose code and are automatically screened against EU sanctions lists, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, and the UN consolidated list; no transaction may be executed to a sanctioned person, entity, or address.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright cash forward with 1–12 month tenors, collateralised by a credit line or cash margin
EUR/GBP outright cash forward for settlement of UK-based engineering counterparties
Cross-currency interest rate swap for project-linked capital and financing inflows
FX swap (swap of principal and interest streams in EUR against USD or GBP) for operational treasury liquidity
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for emerging-market currencies, executed through an authorised international bank desk, subject to Central Bank of Cyprus reporting and mandatory substance documentation
Currency option (European-style, premium-delivered) for capped hedging of major receivables, where availability is determined by the bank's market-risk committee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form HE32) to Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the annual return date (anniversary of incorporation or date of last annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 400 plus per-day default fees; continued non-filing beyond 6 months allows the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of EUR 350 if settled after 30 June but before 31 December; unpaid levy for 3 consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Cyprus private limited companies are required to undergo an independent statutory audit under Companies Law Cap.113; no general turnover-based audit exemption applies to operating offshore engineering/BIM entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the European Union; Cyprus GAAP for limited companies is fully aligned with IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO confirmation filing exists; however, any transfer of shares affecting the ultimate beneficial owner must be reported to the Cyprus Central Beneficial Owners Register within 30 days. The company must also ensure its statutory registers and annual return reflect the current shareholder and UBO position.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–5,000 per year for a small CAD/BIM outsourcing entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate on worldwide income for Cyprus tax-resident companies
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate can be materially reduced: (i) 100% exemption on qualifying dividend income; (ii) 80% exemption on non-business interest and rental income; (iii) IP Box regime producing an effective 2.5% rate on qualifying intangible income under the nexus approach; (iv) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity injected after 1 January 2015; (v) foreign tax credit relief under treaties and unilateral relief; (vi) no withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties. For a CAD/BIM outsourcing entity, the principal benefit is the 12.5% rate with full deduction of payroll, software licences, BIM platform subscriptions, and subcontractor costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR1 (Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically via the Cyprus Tax Department's Tax For All (TFA) / ARIADNE e-portal; attachment of audited financial statements, tax computation, and TP-SIT where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (tax year = calendar year). Separate quarterly VAT returns (VAT Form) and annual Special Defence Contribution (SDC) returns are filed independently; provisional corporate income tax is paid by instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IR1 must be submitted within 12 months after the end of the tax year: for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 31 December of the following year. Provisional (self-assessment) tax instalments fall due on 31 July, 30 September, and 31 December of the tax year, with the fourth instalment on 31 March of the following year; the balancing payment is due together with the filed return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal company name, Tax Identification Code (TIC/TIN), Registrar of Companies registration number (HE number), registered office address, tax year, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name registered with the Cyprus Registrar of Companies; the TIC is the 8-digit TFA identifier. Registered office must be a physical Cyprus address; a P.O. Box is not acceptable. Beneficial owners, even if non-resident, must be disclosed in the UBO register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax per IFRS financial statements; add-back of non-deductible expenses (client entertainment exceeding 50%, fines, taxes, depreciation in excess of capital allowances, non-business provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report CAD/BIM and drafting revenue on a percentage-of-completion basis under IFRS 15; ensure intercompany work-in-progress and accrued income match the audited financial statements accepted by the overseas contracting client.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C – Exempt and deductible income (Boxes 11–15)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: qualifying dividend income (100%); 80% of interest and rental income not derived from normal business activities; certain foreign branch profits; government grants.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not classify engineering service fees, BIM model delivery milestones, or reimbursed travel expenses as exempt passive income; these are business income taxable at 12.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wear-and-tear allowances: IT hardware and BIM/CAD workstations at 20% straight-line; computer software licences at 10% straight-line; motor vehicles at 20% straight-line with annual cost cap; investment allowances apply to certain qualifying assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain an asset register showing the purchase invoices for all workstations, servers, and BIM software; assets acquired from related foreign parties must be at arm's length cost.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward (maximum 5 years) offset against future taxable income; no carry-back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be forfeited if there is a major change in the ownership or nature of trade without commercial justification; any restructuring of the non-resident shareholding should be documented to preserve loss relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 12.5%; deduction of Notional Interest Deduction (NID), IP Box deduction, and foreign tax credit (bilateral or unilateral relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NID applies on new cash or in-kind equity contributed after 1 January 2015; a capital contribution funded by the non-resident parent for BIM equipment can reduce the effective Cyprus rate; keep the contribution documented in board minutes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax assessed less provisional tax instalments paid and any tax credits; balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made from the company's Cyprus bank account; overseas shareholders must not discharge the company's tax liability directly without creating a deemed distribution or benefit-in-kind issue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section H – TP-SIT (Transfer Pricing Summary Information Table)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value and margin of related-party transactions, transfer pricing method applied, functional and risk profile of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an offshore CAD/BIM service provider billing an overseas contracted parent, enter the selected arm's length margin (e.g., TNMM with cost-plus 5–15%), and upload the supporting TP documentation if the €500,000/€750,000 thresholds are exceeded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late electronic filing triggers an administrative fine of €100 per commenced month of delay, capped at €1,200; non-response to TFA compliance notices can attract a further penalty of up to €20,000. Unpaid tax bears interest at 1.5% per month (18.29% effective annual rate) plus an additional charge of 5% where payment is not made within 30 days of assessment. Deliberate misstatement exposes the company to a penalty of up to 100% of the undercharged tax and criminal sanctions (see Fatal Red Flags).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%. Cyprus does not impose any domestic withholding tax on dividends paid by a Cyprus resident company to non-resident shareholders; dividends are paid gross. Cyprus-resident corporate shareholders may instead be subject to Special Defence Contribution (SDC) at 17% on non-exempt dividend income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No administrative relief application is required for outbound dividends to non-residents because the domestic rate is 0%. For inbound dividends (foreign payer → Cyprus company) or where a foreign jurisdiction imposes a residual withholding tax, the Cyprus company must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Cyprus Tax Department via the TFA portal (issued for a calendar year, typically within 5–15 working days) and submit it, together with a completed treaty residence declaration and shareholding evidence, to the foreign payer/foreign tax authority to invoke the Cyprus DTA network. The TRC confirms the company's management and control in Cyprus and is the critical document for claiming treaty benefits abroad.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rate: 0% withholding on outbound royalty and interest payments to non-residents (no Cyprus WHT). Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, interest and royalties paid between associated enterprises of EU member states are exempt from all withholding at source. Where inbound interest/royalties are paid to the Cyprus company from treaty countries, reduced rates of 0%–10% typically apply under Cyprus DTAs, subject to the provision of a Cyprus TRC and beneficial ownership confirmation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000: aggregate value of related-party transactions per tax year triggers mandatory contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation (Local File / Master File aligned to OECD TPG) in Cyprus, with a reduced EUR 250,000 threshold for intra-group financing transactions. A further EUR 750,000 aggregate threshold triggers the mandatory annual TP-SIT filing with Form IR1. Documentation must be submitted to the Tax Commissioner within 30 days of a request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus does not enact a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to offshore centres, but substance is legally required through: (i) the management-and-control test for tax residence (board meetings, strategic decision-making and bank mandates exercised in Cyprus); (ii) the IP Box nexus rule requiring qualifying R&D staff and expenditure in Cyprus; (iii) the EU ATAD-derived General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) empowering the Commissioner to disregard artificial arrangements; and (iv) Cyprus's adherence to the OECD/G20 MLI, which restricts treaty benefits where a principal purpose is treaty shopping. A CAD/BIM company must maintain a physical office, employ technical staff, keep local board minutes and contracts, and demonstrate actual decision-making in Cyprus; a letterbox entity without these elements risks loss of tax residence, re-characterisation as a foreign PE of its shareholder, denial of treaty benefits, or strike-off.
